reasons.C: Best catches the passage's gossipy, self-mocking irony and its jumpy rhythm of clipped asides and short declaratives against longer loquacious runs, with a quoted-servant aside and a teasing close.
reasons.A: Has some of the passage's clipped turns ('That is, I sold him books.', 'Well, then.') and semicolon joins, but the tone is more measured and decorous, and it has less of the passage's playful garrulity.
reasons.B: Plain, earnest and hedging, with evenly paced modern sentences and none of the passage's ironic swagger, fragments or period flourish.
